title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Abdominal pain and lack of bowel movements.

Vitals: BP 138/82, HR 76, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever/chills.
Gastrointestinal: Positive for abdominal distension and lack of flatus.
Neurological: Negative for confusion or weakness.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath.

HPI: Patient is an 89-year-old female who presented with progressive abdominal discomfort. She reported a significant decrease in bowel movements following a recent change in her maintenance medications. She denies severe vomiting or high-grade fever.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for an ileus. Imaging and physical examination confirmed the presence of an ileus without any evidence of a mechanical obstruction. Management focused on conservative measures, including IV fluids and electrolyte correction. The patient responded well to supportive care, and her bowel function returned to baseline.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Ileus

Discharge Medications:
- Metformin 500mg BID
- Lisinopril 10mg QD

Follow-up:
Follow up with primary care physician in 7 days for medication reconciliation and monitoring of gastrointestinal symptoms.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
05/15/2026

distractors.why: It is an ileus, not a mechanical obstruction.
